even to draw it a little out of its position, which, as Lucilla
described afterwards, was like a knife going into her heart.
c1:p33.summary: Dr Marjoribanks sits on and moves his deceased wife's sofa, causing Lucilla acute psychic pain, as if stabbing her heart.
c1:p33.best_quote: he did not hesitate to sit down upon it, and even to draw it a little out of its position, which, as Lucilla described afterwards, was like a knife going into her heart.

matched_quotes.text: Lucilla went about like a sovereign among her people.

c17:p42.text:
And then as the
week drew on towards Thursday, and all her representations proved
unavailing to induce Barbara to get up and prepare herself for her usual
duties, the scorn and vexation and impatience with which the dutiful
little soul met her sister's sullen determination that "she was not
able" to fulfil her ordinary engagements, roused Rose up to a great
resolution. For her own part she was one of the people who do not
understand giving in.
c17:p42.summary: As Thursday approaches and Barbara refuses to rise and attend her duties, Rose resolves to compel her sister to fulfill her obligations despite her distress.

matched_quotes.text: Miss Marjoribanks felt that she could have governed a county without any trouble; and yet she was not able to manage a simple Member of Parliament.

c8:p68.text:
As for a woman in want of
a situation, who had so little common sense as to faint at such a
critical moment, the Rector was disposed to wash his hands of her; for
Mr Bury, "like them all," as Lucilla said, was horribly frightened by a
faint when he saw one, and afterwards pretended to disbelieve it, and
called it one of the things which a little self-command could always
prevent.
c8:p68.summary: Mr Bury, frightened by Mrs Mortimer's fainting, is inclined to deny it happened and blame her lack of self-command.

matched_quotes.text: Always keeping things pleasant' sounds like a compliment.

c22:p45.text:
There was something that
morning in Mr Beverley's tone and manner which struck Lucilla as
something more than usual. She was not a young woman to attach undue
importance to looks and tones; but the Archdeacon's manner was so
softened and mellowed, and his eyes had so much expression in them, and
he looked at Lucilla with such marked regard, that it was impossible for
her not to recognise that a crisis might be approaching.
c22:p45.summary: Lucilla recognises unmistakable signs that the Archdeacon is developing tender feelings towards her and a romantic crisis may approach.
c22:p45.best_quote: the Archdeacon's manner was so softened and mellowed, and his eyes had so much expression in them, and he looked at Lucilla with such marked regard

matched_quotes.text: She writes something to the effect that Lucilla had never relaxed the composure which was so natural to her, that it was almost impossible to tell where the composure ended and the woman began.

c20:p29.text:
At this appeal Mr Cavendish got up again, and began to pace the little
arbour, two steps to the wall, and two steps back again. "I told you I
had almost done it, when that confounded old woman came in," he said:
"that could not be called my fault?"
c20:p29.summary: Mr Cavendish claims he was almost ready to propose when Mrs Chiley interrupted him, absolving himself of blame.

matched_quotes.text: Almost impossible to tell where the composure ended and the woman began.

c35:p23.text:
"I know I am a wretch to be thinking of myself," she said. "She cannot
be expected to stay and sacrifice herself for us, after all she has
suffered. She has made up her mind and advertised in the  Times , and
nothing can change it now. She is going out for a governess, Lucilla."
c35:p23.summary: Rose reveals that Barbara has advertised in the Times to become a governess, a decision nothing can change.

matched_quotes.text: She thinks to herself — and the narrator reports it with complete deadpan gravity — that she has made up her mind to devote herself to her papa and to Carlingford, and that she feels sure it is her vocation.

c4:p37.text:
She succeeded in doing what
is certainly one of the first duties of a woman—she amused her father. He followed her to the drawing-room for a marvel, and took a cup of tea,
though it was against his principles; and, on the whole, Lucilla had the
satisfaction of feeling that she had made a conquest of the Doctor,
which, of course, was the grand and most essential preliminary.
c4:p37.summary: Lucilla succeeds in entertaining her father, making him follow her to the drawing-room and even take tea; she has conquered his affection.
c4:p37.best_quote: She succeeded in doing what is certainly one of the first duties of a woman—she amused her father

matched_quotes.text: There's a moment where the narrator notes, almost in passing, that Lucilla had the satisfaction of knowing she had done her duty — and that this was a satisfaction she rarely failed to secure for herself.

c5:p44.text:
Miss Marjoribanks reflected as she ate—and
indeed, thanks to her perfect health and her agreeable morning walk,
Lucilla had a very pretty appetite, and enjoyed her meal in a way that
would have been most satisfactory to her many friends—that it must be
by way of making his visit, which was aggravating under all
circumstances, more aggravating still, that Tom Marjoribanks had decided
to come now, of all times in the world.
c5:p44.summary: Lucilla reflects that her brother Tom's visit at this critical moment is poorly timed and frustrating.
c5:p44.best_quote: it must be by way of making his visit, which was aggravating under all circumstances, more aggravating still, that Tom Marjoribanks had decided to come now, of all times in the world

matched_quotes.text: She had always felt that Tom would come back — it was in the natural order of things.

c8:p21.text:
She was a great deal too sensible to go into high art
on this occasion, or to electrify her father's friends with her
newly-acquired Italian, or even with German, as some young ladies do. She sang them a ballad out of one of those treasures of resuscitated
ballads which the new generation had then begun to dig out of the bowels
of the earth.
c8:p21.summary: Lucilla wisely avoids displaying advanced musical skills or newly acquired languages, instead singing a resuscitated ballad from the new generation's treasures.

matched_quotes.text: He was a great deal changed, and yet he was Tom.

c3:p16.text:
When you add to a man capable of giving excellent dinners,
like Dr Marjoribanks, another man like young Mr Cavendish, Mrs
Woodburn's brother, who was a wit and a man of fashion, and belonged to
one of the best clubs in town, and brought down gossip with the bloom on
it to Grange Lane; and when you join to Mrs Centum, who was always so
good and so much out of temper that it was safe to calculate on
something amusing from her, the languid but trenchant humour of Mrs
Woodburn—not to speak of their husbands, who were perfectly available
for the background, and all the nephews and cousins and grand-children,
who constantly paid visits to old Mr Western and Colonel Chiley; and the
Browns, when they were at home, with their floating suite of admirers;
and the young ladies who sang, and the young ladies who sketched, and
the men who went out with the hounds, when business permitted them; and
the people who came about the town when there was an election; and the
barristers who made the circuit; and the gay people who came to the
races; not to speak of the varying chances of curates, who could talk or
play the piano, with which Mr Bury favoured his parishioners—for he
changed his curates very often; and the occasional visits of the lesser
county people, and the country clergymen;—it will be plainly apparent
that all that was wanting to Carlingford was a master-hand to blend
these different elements.
c3:p16.summary: The narrator catalogs Carlingford's abundant social assets—excellent dinners, witty figures, entertaining women, visiting relatives, local events, clergy, and county visitors—requiring only masterful coordination.
c3:p16.best_quote: all that was wanting to Carlingford was a master-hand to blend these different elements

matched_quotes.text: With excellent intentions and a great desire to do something for the good of his country.

c5:p17.text:
Lucilla sang her part by herself
gallantly; and when it came to Barbara's turn the second time, Miss
Marjoribanks essayed the second in a false voice, which drove the
contralto off her guard; and then the magnificent volume of sound flowed
forth, grand enough to have filled Lucilla with envy if she had not been
sustained by that sublime confidence in herself which is the first
necessity to a woman with a mission.
c5:p17.summary: Lucilla sings the first part gallantly, deliberately sings the second in a false voice to provoke Barbara into responding, upon which Barbara's magnificent contralto voice flows forth.
c5:p17.best_quote: that sublime confidence in herself which is the first necessity to a woman with a mission

matched_quotes.text: She had fulfilled her mission' — and the very neutrality of that phrase is devastating.

c4:p75.text:
And it was thus that Lucilla made her first bold step out
of the limits of Grange Lane for the good of society, and secured at
once several important personal advantages, and the great charm of those
Thursday evenings which made so entire a revolution in the taste and
ideas of Carlingford.
c4:p75.summary: Through this encounter with Miss Lake, Lucilla takes her first major step beyond her home, initiating the Thursday evenings that will transform Carlingford society.
c4:p75.best_quote: Lucilla made her first bold step out of the limits of Grange Lane for the good of society, and secured at once several important personal advantages, and the great charm of those Thursday evenings which made so entire a revolution in the taste and ideas of Carlingford

c6:p48.text:
"Perhaps I may marry some time," said Miss Marjoribanks, with composure;
"it would be foolish, you know, to make any engagements; but that will
depend greatly upon how you behave, and how Carlingford behaves, papa. I give myself ten years here, if you should be very good. By twenty-nine
I shall be going off a little, and perhaps it may be tiring, for
anything I can tell.
c6:p48.summary: Lucilla calmly announces that marriage depends on her father's and Carlingford's behavior, and that she gives herself ten years to accomplish her objectives before potentially seeking marriage.
c6:p48.best_quote: I give myself ten years here, if you should be very good. By twenty-nine I shall be going off a little, and perhaps it may be tiring, for anything I can tell.

c12:p16.text:
"My dear Barbara," she said, putting her hands on the singer's shoulders
as she finished her strain, "that is enough for to-night. Mr Cavendish
will take you downstairs and get you a cup of tea; for you know there is
no room to-night to serve it upstairs." Thus Miss Marjoribanks proved
herself capable of preferring her great work to her personal sentiments,
which is generally considered next to impossible for a woman.
c12:p16.summary: Lucilla firmly stops Barbara's singing, sending her downstairs with Mr Cavendish for tea, thereby proving herself capable of preferring her great work to personal sentiments.
c12:p16.best_quote: "My dear Barbara, that is enough for to-night. Mr Cavendish will take you downstairs and get you a cup of tea; for you know there is no room to-night to serve it upstairs."

c32:p24.text:
She put her hand
upon his arm sharply, and with a certain energy. "Mr Beverley, Thomas is
behind you with the soup," said Miss Marjoribanks. The Archdeacon turned
round to see what it was, conscious that somebody had spoken to him, but
as indifferent to his companion and to civility as he was to Thomas and
the soup. "What?" he said hoarsely, interrupting his scrutiny for the
moment. But when he had met Miss Marjoribanks's eye the Archdeacon sat
down.
c32:p24.summary: Lucilla firmly redirects the Archdeacon's attention to soup and the servant, bringing him back to social propriety through sheer force of will.
c32:p24.best_quote: Mr Beverley, Thomas is behind you with the soup

c23:p122.text:
She had no more fear of the
result than she had of wetting her feet, which was a thing Mrs Mortimer
and Thomas were both concerned about. But then Lucilla knew her own
resources, and what she was capable of, and proceeded upon her way with
that unconscious calm of genius which is always so inexplicable to the
ordinary world.
c23:p122.summary: The narrator celebrates Lucilla's absolute confidence in her own capabilities and her genius-like calm indifference to doubt.
c23:p122.best_quote: She had no more fear of the result than she had of wetting her feet, which was a thing Mrs Mortimer and Thomas were both concerned about. But then Lucilla knew her own resources, and what she was capable of, and proceeded upon her way with that unconscious calm of genius which is always so inexplicable to the ordinary world.

c27:p51.text:
When the
visitor had finally departed, under the charge of Thomas and Mary Jane,
the father and daughter regarded each other, for the first time, with
dubious glances—for, as far as Lucilla was concerned, it was a
revelation to her of a new and altogether unsuspected danger; and the
Doctor, for his part, was very conciliatory, and showed a certain
consciousness of having committed himself, which made matters twenty
times worse.
c27:p51.summary: After Mrs Mortimer leaves, Lucilla and her father regard each other with dubious glances; she recognizes a new danger, he shows consciousness of transgression.

c27:p60.text:
When the crisis was over she rose up calmly and lighted her
candle, and went to her room with a smile upon her magnanimous lips. As
she performed that simple action, Lucilla had lifted up the feeble
widow, and taken the family of Lakes, and Mr Cavendish, and even the
burly Archdeacon himself, upon her shoulders.
c27:p60.summary: Lucilla rises, lights her candle, and goes to her room having metaphorically taken all her protégés upon her shoulders.
c27:p60.best_quote: As she performed that simple action, Lucilla had lifted up the feeble widow, and taken the family of Lakes, and Mr Cavendish, and even the burly Archdeacon himself, upon her shoulders.

c28:p89.text:
And
it was thus, with Miss Marjoribanks leaning on his arm, and General
Travers, in all the warmth of renewed friendship, guarding him on the
other side, that Mr Cavendish, whose head was in a whirl of excitement,
and who did not know what he was doing, was led back in triumph past
Colonel Chiley's very door, where the Archdeacon was lying in wait to
crunch his bones, back from all his aberrations into the very heart of
Grange Lane.
c28:p89.summary: Cavendish is led in triumph by Lucilla and General Travers past the Archdeacon's position and back to Grange Lane, fully restored under Lucilla's influence.
c28:p89.best_quote: And it was thus, with Miss Marjoribanks leaning on his arm, and General Travers, in all the warmth of renewed friendship, guarding him on the other side, that Mr Cavendish, whose head was in a whirl of excitement, and who did not know what he was doing, was led back in triumph past Colonel Chiley's very door, where the Archdeacon was lying in wait to crunch his bones, back from all his aberrations into the very heart of Grange Lane.

c30:p7.text:
But when he was delivered from that danger,
something still more formidable awaited the unfortunate man. He could
not believe his eyes at first, nor conceive it possible that Fate would
have such a spite against him; but there was no mistaking the crumpled
dress, any more than the straight eyebrows and flashing oblique glances
that had already found him out.
c30:p7.summary: Mr Cavendish is startled to see Barbara appear on Grange Lane, recognizing her as a serious complication.
c30:p7.best_quote: there was no mistaking the crumpled dress, any more than the straight eyebrows and flashing oblique glances that had already found him out

c30:p15.text:
"Yes, I am going to see Miss Marjoribanks," he said, with a face
which extremity rendered stolid and impassible. As for poor Barbara, her
colour changed in a moment. The very least that she had a right to
expect was that he should have asked her pardon, put himself at her
feet; and her mingled spite and humiliation and mortification at this
response were beyond telling.
c30:p15.summary: Mr Cavendish admits his intention to visit Lucilla, shocking Barbara into an emotional transformation from manipulative to devastated.
c30:p15.best_quote: Yes, I am going to see Miss Marjoribanks
